The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $N\ge2$. A fixed massive rest representation fiber consists here of a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathcal K$, a number $M>0$ with $P^0=MI$ and $P^j=0$, and scalar central charges $Z^{IJ}=z^{IJ}I$, where $Z=(z^{IJ})$ is the complex antisymmetric $N\times N$ matrix in the four-dimensional algebra with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\epsilon_{12}=1$. Suppose the charge operators and their actual Hilbert adjoints have a common dense invariant domain $\mathcal D$ on the fiber and every product in the expanded anticommutators is defined there. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $M$ and each $z^{IJ}$ have mass dimension one. For $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_N)\in\mathbb C^N$ define $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_I|v_I|^2$ and for $u,v\in\mathbb C^N$ put $u^*Zv=\sum_{I,J}\bar u_Iz^{IJ}v_J$. Define

$$\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Zv\|_2.$$

Then $M\ge\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. For $N=2$, write $z=z^{12}$, so $Z=\begin{pmatrix}0&z\\-z&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|z|$. If $z=e^{i\phi}|z|$ (with any $\phi$ when $z=0$), define on $\mathcal D$

$$A:=Q^1_1-e^{i\phi}(Q^2_2)^*,\qquad A^\sharp:=(Q^1_1)^*-e^{-i\phi}Q^2_2.$$

The algebraic anticommutator $AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A$ equals $4(M-|z|)I$ on $\mathcal D$. Here $A^\sharp$ is the displayed combination of the individual actual adjoints; it is not asserted to be the adjoint of an unbounded sum on its maximal domain. If $\mathcal K$ is finite-dimensional, all charge domains equal $\mathcal K$ and $A^\sharp=A^*$, so the formula is the ordinary operator anticommutator. At saturation $M=|z|$, for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$ one has $A\psi=A^\sharp\psi=0$. This is a representation-theoretic fiber statement: it does not assert that the fixed-momentum fiber is a normalizable subspace of the full Hilbert space, or that a state with specified charge exists or is stable.

Assume Countable Choice. Use the complex Hilbert-space convention that the inner product is linear in its first variable and conjugate-linear in its second. Let $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\sigma^0=I_2$, $\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Define $\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)=\{H\in M_2(\mathbb C):H^\dagger=H\}$ and $\Phi:\mathbb R^{1,3}\to\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)$ by $\Phi(x)=-\sigma^\mu x_\mu$. For $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)=\{g\in M_2(\mathbb C):\det g=1\}$, define $\Lambda_g$ by $\Phi(\Lambda_gx)=g\Phi(x)g^\dagger$; the real-linear map $\Phi$ is an isomorphism because $I_2,\sigma^1,\sigma^2,\sigma^3$ form a basis of $\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)$, and $\det\Phi(x)=-\eta_{\mu\nu}x^\mu x^\nu$ is preserved. Congruence by $g$ preserves positive-semidefinite Hermitian matrices, so $\Lambda_g$ preserves the chosen future cone. Let $\Lambda_g^\vee$ be the dual action on covectors, $(\Lambda_g^\vee p)(x)=p(\Lambda_g^{-1}x)$. The spin-cover Poincare group is $\mathcal P=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)\ltimes_\Lambda\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with product $(g,a)(h,b)=(gh,a+\Lambda_gb)$.

A **positive unitary super-Poincare representation** in this item is the following data. It includes a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a bounded self-adjoint grading $\Gamma$ with $\Gamma^2=I$, and a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of $\mathcal P$ commuting with $\Gamma$. It also includes a regular projection-valued measure $E$ on the Borel subsets of the covector space $(\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ such that

$$U(1,a)=\Phi_E(p\mapsto e^{i p(a)}),\qquad U(g,0)E(B)U(g,0)^*=E(\Lambda_g^\vee B),\qquad E(\mathcal C_+^*)=I,$$

where $\Phi_E$ is the bounded Borel PVM integral, $\mathcal C_+^*=\{p:p^0=-p_0\ge |\vec p|\}$ is the closed future cone in covector coordinates, and $p(a)=p_\mu a^\mu$. The PVM functional calculus makes every translation unitary commute with every $E(B)$. For each coordinate define the self-adjoint translation generator

$$P_\mu=p_\mu(E),\qquad D(P_\mu)=\left\{\psi\in\mathcal H:\int |p_\mu|^2\,dE_\psi(p)<\infty\right\},\qquad E_\psi(B)=\langle E(B)\psi,\psi\rangle.$$

Here $p_\mu(E)$ is the unbounded PVM integral with its truncation domain; the real-valued integral is self-adjoint under Countable Choice. Thus $P^0=\eta^{0\nu}P_\nu$ is nonnegative. The joint PVM is part of the representation data; no joint spectral measure is inferred from formal commutators on a dense domain.

For each $I,\alpha$, the supercharge $Q^I_\alpha$ is a closed densely defined operator on $\mathcal H$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}=(Q^I_\alpha)^*$ is its actual Hilbert adjoint, with exactly the adjoint domain. The central generators $Z^{IJ}$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}$ are represented by closed densely defined operators with $\bar Z_{IJ}=(Z^{IJ})^*$ as an actual Hilbert adjoint. On a common dense graded linear domain $\mathcal D$, contained in the domains of every generator product in the bracket table, the operator supercommutator is the displayed algebra bracket. In particular,

$$\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\delta^I{}_J,\qquad \{Q^I_\alpha,Q^J_\beta\}=2\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}Z^{IJ},\qquad \{\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I},\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=2\epsilon_{\dot\alpha\dot\beta}\bar Z_{IJ}.$$

The domain $\mathcal D$ is invariant under those generators and under $U(\mathcal P)$. The even group acts on the charge domains exactly: for every $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$, conjugation by $U(g,0)$ sends each closed charge to the corresponding fundamental or dotted spinor transform as an equality of operators, including equality of domains. The central generators transform as Lorentz scalars, commute with translations, and commute on $\mathcal D$ with all supercharges; these relations also include their domain invariance.

For every Borel set $B\subseteq(\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ and every charge $Q$ or $Q^*$, require the reducing-projection/domain conditions

$$E(B)D(Q)\subseteq D(Q),\qquad Q E(B)\psi=E(B)Q\psi\quad(\psi\in D(Q)),$$

and the same conditions with $Q^*$ in place of $Q$. Require also $\Gamma E(B)=E(B)\Gamma$ for every Borel $B$. In particular this supplies integrated translation covariance with domain invariance; a relation $[P_\mu,Q]=0$ on a common core alone is not substituted for it. A closed graded subspace $K$ is invariant when $U(g,a)K=K$ for all $(g,a)\in\mathcal P$ and each charge and adjoint maps $D(Q)\cap K$ into $K$, with those intersections dense in $K$. The representation is irreducible when its only such invariant subspaces are $\{0\}$ and $\mathcal H$.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a selected pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills model whose global gauge group is $SU(2)$.
The microscopic matter-hypermultiplet index set is empty, as explicitly adopted in the independent pure-model postulate. In $\mathcal N=1$ language the gauge sector is one vector superfield and one adjoint chiral superfield with scalar $\phi\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, connection normalization $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$, positive dimensionless gauge coupling $g$, zero chiral superpotential and no ultraviolet matter mass. The low-energy charged monopole fields introduced later are emergent infrared fields, not an ultraviolet hypermultiplet. This is the selected physical datum, not a specialization inferred from the different one-hypermultiplet postulate.

A **classical Coulomb-branch configuration** is a constant adjoint scalar
configuration satisfying the model's zero auxiliary-field conditions, taken
modulo the compact $SU(2)$ gauge action. This uses the compact-group orbit
quotient in the preceding vacuum-moduli definition; it does not replace that
quotient by a complexified-group stability construction. In the
weak-coupling semiclassical frame, let $a$ be the eigenvalue coordinate fixed
by $\phi=\tfrac12\operatorname{diag}(a,-a)$, of mass dimension one. When a quantum
theory with a vacuum-moduli set has actually been constructed, the **quantum
Coulomb-branch coordinate** $u$ denotes the chosen gauge-invariant chiral
quadratic-operator expectation value in the source trace normalization for
which the weak-coupling relation is $u=a^2/2$. Its mass dimension is two.
This definition does not assert that $u$ globally parameterizes the quantum
vacua.

On an open patch $U$ of the $u$-plane where the period functions are
holomorphic and the local gauge-coupling matrix has positive imaginary part,
an **electric/magnetic frame** means a chosen ordered basis of the formal
charge lattice that fixes local cycle representatives. Their period
functions are the complex electric coordinate $a:U\to\mathbb C$ and complex
dual coordinate $a_D:U\to\mathbb C$, both of mass dimension one. The local
two-derivative abelian gauge action is encoded by a holomorphic
**prepotential** $\mathcal F_U(a)$ of mass dimension two, defined on that
patch by

$$a_D=\frac{\partial\mathcal F_U}{\partial a},\qquad \tau=\frac{\partial a_D}{\partial a}=\frac{\partial^2\mathcal F_U}{\partial a^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0.$$

The dimensionless $\tau$ is the local complexified gauge coupling; changing
the electric/magnetic frame changes the pair $(a_D,a)$ by the corresponding
integral linear transformation and may require a different local
prepotential. Thus neither period is asserted to be a single-valued global
function on a punctured branch.

For this source-normalized data, define the **formal electric/magnetic charge
label lattice** to be $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with a label
$(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}(u;n_e,n_m)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The pair labels
the central-charge formula; the lattice definition does not assert that every
label is an allowed line operator, a dynamical particle, a stable state, or a
state in any constructed Hilbert space. Those are separate model data.

The word **exact** in this page refers only to the adopted source-proposed
Wilsonian two-derivative low-energy data on a regular patch of the selected
pure SU(2) model. It does not mean a proof of a nonperturbative continuum
path integral, a global single-valued prepotential, or an exact statement
about arbitrary $\mathcal N=2$ theories.

Adopt the source-proposed low-energy solution data for pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills with global gauge group $SU(2)$, one
adjoint vector multiplet, rank one, no matter hypermultiplets, and the coupling, units, connection-normalized scalar, and prepotential convention of the independent pure ultraviolet vector-multiplet datum. Use natural units
$c=\hbar=1$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a positive
dynamical scale $\Lambda$ of mass dimension one. The gauge-invariant
coordinate $u$ has mass dimension two; set $w=u/\Lambda^2$.

The absence of microscopic hypermultiplets is an explicit model input in that independent ultraviolet postulate. The charged monopole hypermultiplet in a local infrared frame below is emergent; it does not change the ultraviolet matter content.

On the regular $w$-plane with singular values $w=1,-1,\infty$ removed,
adopt the family of genus-one curves, where $x,y,w$ are dimensionless:

$$\Sigma_w:\quad y^2=(x-1)(x+1)(x-w).$$

and the meromorphic period differential

$$\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}=\frac{\sqrt2\Lambda}{2\pi}\frac{y\,dx}{x^2-1}.$$

Within this proposed solution, take the quantum vacuum-moduli data to be the
entire $u$-plane, with a $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry $u\mapsto-u$ and singular
values $u=\Lambda^2,-\Lambda^2,\infty$. This is part of the adopted
solution ansatz, not a consequence of a constructed continuum theory.

For a chosen local cycle basis $\gamma_m,\gamma_e$ on $\Sigma_w$ with
intersection number $\gamma_m\cdot\gamma_e=1$, define
$a_D=\oint_{\gamma_m}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and
$a=\oint_{\gamma_e}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$. These periods have mass
dimension one, are multivalued under continuation around the punctures, and
are used in the local prepotential convention
$a_D=\partial\mathcal F/\partial a$ and
$\tau=\partial^2\mathcal F/\partial a^2$ with
$\operatorname{Im}\tau>0$. In the source's counterclockwise-loop
convention, the period column $(a_D,a)^T$ has monodromy matrices

$$M_\infty=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_+=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_-=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}.$$

Adopt the source's formal charge-label lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and central-charge pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}=n_ea+n_ma_D$ for labels
$(n_e,n_m)\in\mathbb Z^2$. In the supersymmetry convention of this page,
the scalar central charge is normalized as
$z=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}$. The mass inequality and its
saturation statement are separate theorem deductions. No claim is made that
every lattice label is an allowed line operator or is represented by a stable
particle.

Adopt the singularity interpretation that the $w=1$ point has a light
monopole with $a_D=0$, while the $w=-1$ point has a light dyon with
$a-a_D=0$ in the chosen frame. These are source-proposed physical inputs
tested by their monodromies; they are not deduced here from a constructed
continuum theory.
In the local monopole patch, adopt the dual $U(1)_D$ field content and superpotential described in the preceding effective-model definition. The source two-derivative vector metric is positive and generally field dependent, determined by the local dual coupling; a regulated matching scale is part of any effective action with the light monopole retained. That definition explicitly freezes this metric at $b=g_D^{-2}>0$ for the subsequent classical calculations. Metric freezing, and the further replacement of $u(A_D)$ by its linear Taylor term where explicitly requested, are additional approximations, not exact identities of the full period solution. No bound on their discarded corrections is adopted here. A small N=1-breaking mass parameter $\mu$ of
mass dimension one adds the local superpotential term $\mu u(A_D)$ to
$\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M$. The local description applies only near this
singularity, below its effective cutoff, and does not simultaneously describe
the mutually nonlocal dyon at the other singularity.

Here **exact low-energy solution** means the adopted two-derivative
Wilsonian data of this source-defined model on its regular patches. It does
not mean a proof of a nonperturbative UV path integral, a global
single-valued prepotential, or an identity for arbitrary gauge groups,
matter contents, or N=2 theories.

rest fiber: neither [F1] nor the period pairing asserts that the selected

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Reflection of the second transverse coordinate proves $E_0\ge2\pi\xi|n|$ for negative n. Step 2.1 now proves the claimed positive bound for every full-model profile. No full-circle boundary-current limit was assumed or inferred from finite energy.

Let $N=|n|$. Choose smooth radial functions f,h with f(r) equal to a positive constant times $r^N$ near zero, h(r) equal to a constant times $r^2$ near zero, and f=h=1 outside one fixed disk; choose the near-zero coefficients as smooth functions of $r^2$ and interpolate on a compact annulus. Set $q=\sqrt\xi f(r)e^{in\theta}$, $p=a=0$, and $A=nh(r)d\theta$, hence $M=q/\sqrt2$, $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}\bar q/\sqrt2$. The charged fields are smooth at zero because $r^Ne^{in\theta}$ is $z^N$ or $\bar z^N$, and the connection is smooth because $r^2d\theta=x^1dx^2-x^2dx^1$. Curvature and every non-vacuum energy term are supported in a fixed disk; all are smooth there. Outside it the field is exactly in the vacuum orbit, the covariant gradients vanish and the angular flux coefficient is n. Thus this is an admitted finite-energy profile. Its energy is positive by step 3.1 and finite directly; consequently $0<\gamma2\pi\xi|n|\le\tau_n<\infty$.

For any profile, M is nonzero outside a disk by uniform vacuum approach. The circle-valued function $(M/|M|)e^{-in\theta}$ has degree zero on that exterior annulus. It has a smooth real phase lift $\chi$: the closed real one-form $-if^{-1}df$ for this circle-valued function f has zero integral on each circle, so integrating first radially and then angularly from a fixed base point defines a smooth periodic lift with $e^{i\chi}=f$. Multiply $-\chi$ by a radial smooth cutoff equal to zero near the inner boundary and one on a larger exterior annulus, then exponentiate to obtain a globally smooth gauge transformation. The transformed fields have $M=m e^{in\theta}$, m>0, and $A=nd\theta+\alpha$ outside a compact set. This gauge change leaves energy and the original angular condition invariant and fixes the exact exterior M-phase; it does not impose a new decay hypothesis. Write $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}w e^{-in\theta}$, so m,w tend uniformly to v.

On this exterior, s is bounded below by $\xi/2$ and m by $v/2$. The potential controls $|a|^2\le V_b/\xi$, $d^2\le2b_+V_b$, $|H|^2\le b_+V_b$ and $(s-\xi)^2\le C_VV_b$. Since $m^2-v^2=(s+d-\xi)/2$, $|m-v|^2\le[(s-\xi)^2+d^2]/(2v^2)$ is integrable. Also $m w-v^2=e^{-i\beta}[H-\mu(u'(a)-c)]/\sqrt2$, so $|w-v|\le(2/v)\{(|H|+K|a|)/\sqrt2+v|m-v|\}$ is square-integrable. Thus a,m-v,w-v are in $L^2$ on the exterior. Finally $DM=e^{in\theta}(dm-im\alpha)$, with dm and alpha real. Its squared norm is $|dm|^2+m^2|\alpha|^2$, so finite charged energy and m>=v/2 give $\alpha,dm\in L^2$. On compact sets all fields and coefficients are smooth and bounded. Hence any two canonical profiles differ in $L^2$ in a,M,$\widetilde M$ and their connection one-forms. These mass-tail conclusions use uniform approach to the vacuum as well as the finite potential/kinetic energy; finite energy alone was not asserted to force pointwise vacuum approach.

Let two canonical profiles be given and choose one radius beyond both cleanup disks. A smooth cutoff $\eta(t)$, t in [0,ell], constant zero near 0 and one near ell, defines an explicit collar by linearly blending a,M,$\widetilde M$,A_1,A_2 and setting $A_3=0$. The neutral disk is convex, so the blend stays in it. Longitudinal scalar derivatives and $F_{3i}$ are $\eta'$ times the corresponding $L^2$ differences from step 6.1, hence have finite energy. For either charged field f, its transverse covariant derivative along the blend equals the blend of the two original covariant derivatives plus a bounded coefficient times $(A^{(1)}-A^{(0)})(f^{(1)}-f^{(0)})$. The connection difference is $L^2$ and the field difference is bounded globally, so this term is $L^2$; neutral gradients and transverse curvatures also blend linearly. Near infinity the field deviations from the common canonical vacuum frame are $L^2$ and uniformly small. Smoothness of u,b and vanishing of the potential and its first derivatives on that vacuum orbit give the uniform local estimate $V_b\le C(|a|^2+|m-v|^2+|w-v|^2)$ along the blend, by a Taylor formula on one compact transverse slice of the phase orbit. This makes the collar potential integrable; compact interiors have finite energy by smoothness. The exterior M-phase remains exactly $e^{in\theta}$ because its blended amplitude is positive, and $A_\theta-n$ is a convex blend of two functions tending uniformly to zero. Thus winding, angular condition and limiting flux are preserved on every collar slice; uniform covariant-gradient decay is preserved by the same product formula, using $\alpha\to0$ from $DM\to0$ and m>=v/2. This constructs an actual finite-energy collar, with cost independent of any later cylinder length L.

The three-dimensional energy is the transverse planar energy on each slice plus nonnegative longitudinal Maxwell and scalar terms. By [F4] and the definition of $\tau_n$, every competitor has $E_{b,3}\ge\tau_nL$. For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the definition of the finite infimum provides one planar profile with energy below $\tau_n+\varepsilon$; gauge-clean it by step 5.1. Step 7.1 constructs collars from each fixed end trace to this profile, with one chosen width ell and finite total energy $C_\varepsilon$, independent of L. Concatenate the collars with its translation-invariant extension over length L-2ell. This is a smooth admissible competitor because each collar is constant near the inner face, and it has energy at most $(\tau_n+\varepsilon)(L-2\ell)+C_\varepsilon$. Taking the infimum proves the two-sided bounds. Dividing by L, taking limsup as L tends to infinity and then allowing each $\varepsilon>0$ to tend to zero gives limsup<=tau_n, while the lower bound gives liminf>=tau_n. Hence the limit is tau_n>0. No minimizer or uniform bound on $C_\varepsilon$ as epsilon tends to zero is used, so no generic $O(1)$ remainder follows.

In this specified magnetostatic model all time derivatives and $A_0$ vanish, so the electric field is zero and the charged time-current density vanishes. With constant or absent theta, the Gauss constraint is therefore zero on every constructed trial field, including collars, even when b varies spatially. The slice lower bound remains true on any further constraint subset. In the adopted charge dictionary, the fixed dual magnetic flux is original electric flux, so its positive asymptotic energy per separation proves the stated classical local confinement. It supplies neither the different Gauss law with field-dependent theta nor a statement about arbitrary quantum line operators or microscopic string-breaking processes.
